llm_expert_review.summary: The Unity Catalog metadata is in strong foundational health, with 100% coverage on both table and column descriptions and all four analyzed tables having primary keys defined. However, a critical gap exists: there are zero existing SQL queries registered, which is a significant readiness concern for Databricks Genie's ability to generate accurate and contextually relevant SQL out of the box.
llm_expert_review.genie_impact_analysis: The absence of any existing SQL queries (RED status) is the most impactful gap for Genie readiness. Genie relies heavily on curated example queries — often called 'Genie-approved' or trusted SQL samples — to learn domain-specific patterns, business logic, metric definitions, and preferred join paths. Without these, Genie must infer intent purely from descriptions and schema structure, which increases the risk of generating syntactically valid but semantically incorrect SQL (e.g., wrong aggregation logic, incorrect filter conditions, or suboptimal join strategies). Additionally, only 1 of 4 tables has foreign key relationships defined, meaning Genie has limited explicit relationship context to guide multi-table joins, further compounding the query generation risk in the absence of example SQL to compensate.
recommended_next_steps: Immediately curate and register a library of at least 10–20 validated, business-representative SQL queries as Genie trusted assets — prioritizing queries that cover common KPIs, frequent join patterns across all 4 tables, and key filtering/aggregation logic used by business stakeholders.

Define foreign key relationships for the remaining 3 tables that currently lack FK constraints, so Genie has explicit, machine-readable join path guidance to supplement the missing example queries and reduce multi-table join errors.

Engage business analysts and data consumers to document the top 5–10 most frequently asked business questions, then translate each into a validated SQL query and register it within the Genie Space as an approved example to accelerate contextual learning.
After adding example queries and FK relationships, re-run the metadata quality pre-analysis to confirm all dimensions reach GREEN status before promoting the Genie Space to production business users.

semantic_validation.actual_answer: El número de órdenes por segmento de mercado varía según los datos. Por ejemplo, el segmento 'AUTOMOBILE' podría tener 29,752 órdenes, 'BUILDING' 27,631, 'FURNITURE' 28,144, 'HOUSEHOLD' 28,823 y 'MACHINERY' 27,650 (valores hipotéticos ilustrativos). La consulta SQL proporcionada calculará los valores reales.
semantic_validation.generated_sql:
SELECT
    c.market_segment,
    COUNT(DISTINCT f.order_id) AS total_orders
FROM
    brz_dev.default.fact_sales_demo_genie f
    JOIN brz_dev.default.dim_customer_demo_genie c
        ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.market_segment
ORDER BY
    total_orders DESC;
semantic_validation.reasoning: La pregunta solicita el conteo de órdenes agrupadas por segmento de mercado. La tabla de hechos 'fact_sales_demo_genie' contiene el campo 'order_id' (identificador de orden) y 'customer_id' (para enlazar con el cliente). La dimensión 'dim_customer_demo_genie' contiene el campo 'market_segment'. Mediante un JOIN entre ambas tablas por 'customer_id' y usando COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) agrupado por 'market_segment', se puede responder la pregunta de forma completa y precisa. No hay ambigüedad ni datos faltantes.

consolidated_mv_design.consolidation_reasoning: A single central view built on the sales fact table, joined to customer, product, and date dimensions, provides all the necessary context to answer the business question about order counts by market segment. The view exposes the market_segment dimension from dim_customer and a distinct order count measure from the fact table, enabling direct aggregation by segment.

proposed_yaml_config.comment: Vista semántica central de ventas. Combina la tabla de hechos de ventas con las dimensiones de cliente, producto y fecha para permitir análisis de órdenes, ingresos y descuentos por segmento de mercado, producto, marca, fabricante y período de tiempo.

dimensions.name: Segmento de Mercado
dimensions.comment: Segmento de mercado al que pertenece el cliente que realizó la orden.

dimensions.name: Tipo de Producto
dimensions.comment: Tipo o categoría del producto vendido.

dimensions.name: Año
dimensions.comment: Año calendario en que se realizó la venta.

dimensions.name: Mes
dimensions.comment: Nombre del mes en que se realizó la venta.

measures.name: Número de Órdenes
measures.comment: Cantidad de órdenes únicas. Una orden puede contener múltiples líneas de producto.

measures.name: Ventas Brutas
measures.comment: Suma del valor bruto de ventas antes de aplicar descuentos.

measures.name: Ventas Netas
measures.comment: Suma del valor neto de ventas después de aplicar descuentos.

measures.name: Descuento Total
measures.comment: Suma total de descuentos aplicados a las líneas de venta.
